headline: High: Firecrawl’s broad network/API and API-key handling can amplify Argo Workflows outputs into data leakage and compliance risk; prompt-injection risk is limited by lack of a direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows has no browser and only allowlisted egress, while Firecrawl exposes MCP/API scraping and can ingest web content. There is no documented shared channel or direct output ingestion path between them, so prompt injection is not default. The main pathway would require manual bridging or an orchestrator wiring Argo outputs into Firecrawl inputs.
conditions: IF an operator pipes Argo-produced text into Firecrawl prompts or scrape inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, content-based hijacking becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pass raw Argo outputs into Firecrawl prompts.
Add a manual review step before any Firecrawl action.
Disable any shared clipboard or queue integration.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all cross-agent payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters, and Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys with broad egress. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can leak sensitive artifacts if Argo outputs are forwarded into Firecrawl or if Firecrawl is used on those artifacts. The uncertainty about the exact integration path pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Argo artifacts contain secrets or regulated data and are sent to Firecrawl, leakage occurs.
IF Firecrawl is configured to scrape internal URLs or uploaded artifacts, those contents can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Restrict Firecrawl to non-sensitive URLs.
Redact secrets from Argo artifacts before handoff.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
Review outbound requests for sensitive payloads.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists at the orchestrator boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows is a workflow engine with REST/gRPC APIs, and Firecrawl supports multiple instances plus API/CLI/MCP use. The profiles do not show shared filesystem writes, git state, or overlapping mutable resources, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty remains because both can be orchestrated concurrently and Firecrawl is runnable.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator shares a single output directory between them, file clobbering becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Use per-agent credentials.
Avoid concurrent mutation of the same API objects.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce artifacts and parameters that Firecrawl may consume through API/MCP workflows, and Firecrawl’s scraping/extraction outputs are often treated as structured downstream inputs. There is no documented verification gate between them, so a bad Argo output can cascade into Firecrawl actions or reports. The pair is not proven to auto-act, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl consumes Argo-generated URLs, prompts, or parameters without validation, errors propagate.
IF downstream automation trusts Firecrawl outputs as authoritative, incorrect upstream data can trigger bad actions.
mitigations: Validate Argo outputs before handoff.
Require schema checks on Firecrawl inputs.
Add a human review step for high-impact actions.
Log and compare source URLs against expected allowlists.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before acting on extracted data.

E_compliance.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters, while Firecrawl handles web content, screenshots, and API keys and is a networked service. If regulated or EU personal data is routed from Argo into Firecrawl, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safe assumption is a policy mismatch risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF EU personal data or PHI is processed by both agents, compliance review is required.
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the workflow store and Firecrawl logs, subject-rights handling can fail.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Avoid routing regulated data through Firecrawl.
Align retention settings across systems.
Document residency for all outbound requests.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
